simulator_description: This simulator generates single-stage Beer Game (SUPPLY) trajectories where a retailer-like node evolves over discrete time with nonnegative inventory, backlog (unmet demand carried forward), and a shipment pipeline represented as quantity/remaining-lead-time pairs. Each step optionally receives pipeline arrivals (counting down lead times), realizes stochastic customer demand from a count process (Poisson or overdispersed Gamma-Poisson/Negative Binomial), fulfills demand/backlog subject to inventory and a backlog-vs-demand service priority parameter, and places a replenishment order that enters the pipeline with stochastic quantity noise and a categorical lead time over 1–5 periods. A categorical “update convention” parameter randomizes the order of arrivals, fulfillment, and ordering to match different operational timing assumptions; using probabilistic choices, explicit pipeline countdown, and invariant checks (no negative stock/backlog) makes the structure consistent with standard Beer Game mechanics while keeping dynamics stochastic and identifiable for calibration.
